name: Iron (Fe)
summary: An essential mineral central to haemoglobin and myoglobin oxygen transport, and to many enzymes. Both deficiency and overload cause disease.

conditions.label: Deficiency
conditions.description: The most common nutritional deficiency worldwide; limits haemoglobin synthesis.

affects.detail: Low iron limits haem synthesis, producing small, pale red cells with fatigue, pallor and reduced exercise tolerance.

genderModifiers.female: Menstrual blood loss and pregnancy raise iron demand, making deficiency notably more common in menstruating and pregnant people.

ageModifiers.infant: Rapid growth and low iron stores make infants and toddlers especially vulnerable; deficiency can impair neurodevelopment.
ageModifiers.child: Iron deficiency in childhood is linked to impaired cognition and attention.

affects.effect: Tachycardia and, if severe, high-output strain
affects.detail: To compensate for low oxygen-carrying capacity the heart rate rises; chronic severe anaemia strains the heart.
Iron is a cofactor for dopamine synthesis; deficiency is associated with restless legs syndrome and reduced concentration.

conditions.label: Overload (haemochromatosis)
conditions.description: Chronic iron overload deposits iron in parenchymal organs, generating oxidative damage.

affects.detail: Iron accumulation in hepatocytes drives fibrosis, cirrhosis and increased liver-cancer risk.
Iron deposition in pancreatic islets impairs insulin secretion, causing diabetes.
Myocardial iron loading causes dilated/restrictive cardiomyopathy and conduction disturbance.
Iron and melanin deposition gives a characteristic bronze skin discolouration.
